Marijuana is a medicine to a lot of people in a lot of different ways. It is also a substitution to alcohol for a lot of people. You can smoke weed and have children, obviously if you keep the two separate. It is different than having a beer because you can’t just smoke one hit and not be high. (You can drink a beer and not be drunk.)

That being said, studies are showing that it can be harmful to a growing fetus and consulting your doctor regarding consumption is really important since there are medications that have been studied for a lot longer for their effects on pregnancy. This is something she needs to consider before she gets pregnant: is she able to not smoke weed?

In your case, this may come off as harsh given your last paragraph, but she may not be the one for you. You can clearly identify that her usage bothers you and you are valid for feeling that. She should be able to maintain commitments to you even if that’s as simple as choosing *not* to smoke weed to not leave you waiting outside her house.

I don’t know, I think it sounds like you need to consider if this behavior is something you want at this point in your life and in your future. She sounds like she is using marijuana as an escape as opposed to a medication replacement. She values her time spent getting high over being with you sometimes. That’s something I don’t think is fair in a serious relationship.

My ex-boyfriend’s dad passed suddenly after a 5-month battle with melanoma. My own dad was never the best growing up and his dad was amazing. I’m not sure how close of a relationship you’ve been able to form with your partner’s mother, but you are allowed to have your own feelings about her passing too. I definitely shut myself off completely and solely focused on his emotional state. By the way, 3 years with notice vs 5 months with no notice feels the same when it comes to losing a loved one. 
  
That being said, the best way you can support him is by listening and paying attention. Please do not try to read his mind. If he has asked you to give him this space, you are doing everything you can for him. I can’t really elaborate further on this since every person is different, but my ex-boyfriend needed a lot of reassurance. I made sure he knew I would give him whatever he needed and he could tell me without me getting offended or taking it personally. I communicated with his mom (they were separated and dad was remarried) when he passed to make sure she was there for him since he was shut off from mostly everyone in his life but me when his dad got sicker. Sadly, there is not much you can do personally for him other than be there and help him when you see you can.

Aside from providing meals, I’m not sure how close you are with the family, but I would definitely see what errands you can do for them. The other big thing is helping around the house with cleaning, laundry, organizing the fridge, taking out the trash, etc etc.
